Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

old adjective

of people: aged

also elderly, aged, old people, get old, senior citizen, senior citizens, seniors, the elderly, oldster

classical

Cic. Sen. 25: quamvīs sit senex

senex, senis

adjective and noun, third declension; comparative senior

old; an old man

Of an old person, man or woman, and as a noun an old man (see old man); an old woman is anus (see old woman). “Get old” is senēscere.

Other words

  • grandis nātū — advanced in years

    also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 63: grandis nātū

    Polite and a little formal, like “elderly”. Grandis alone is “big, full-grown” (see big).

  • vetulus, vetula, vetulum — oldish; a little old man or woman

    also used · classical · Cato Agr. 2.7: bovēs vetulōs (Lewis & Short, s.v. senex); Lewis & Short s.v. vetulus

    The diminutive of vetus, affectionate or slighting.

  • longaevus, longaeva, longaevum — aged, of great age

    also used · classical · Verg. A. 3.169 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 77

    (vōx poētica: Verg., Ov.)

Examples

  • nec vērō dubitat agricola, quamvīs sit senex, quaerentī cui serat respondēre: ‘dīs immortālibus’

    nor does the farmer, however old he is, hesitate to answer one who asks whom he is planting for: ‘for the immortal gods’Cic. Sen. 25

  • cōnsurrēxisse omnēs illī dīcuntur et senem sessum recēpisse

    they all stood up, it is said, and made room for the old man to sitCic. Sen. 63

See also old man, old woman, older, how old are you?, old, young.
